chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who instructed that Hajj al-Islam be performed on his behalf, but he left only fifty dirhams in total. He said: Hajj will be performed on his behalf from some of the stations that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) designated, from the nearby ones, so as not to contradict the first report. For the reasoning in this report is that we apply it to the one upon whom Hajj was obligatory, but he delayed it, then died without performing Hajj al-Islam. In that case, Hajj is performed on his behalf from some of the stations, because that runs the course of a debt upon him, and he left only the amount of what is due upon him, so his debt is paid with it. And the first report applies to the one upon whom Hajj was not obligatory; therefore, whatever of that specified amount he leaves, his heirs are more entitled to it, because nothing was obligatory upon him that needed to be paid on his behalf.

key_terms.دَيْنٍ: Debt (used here to describe the obligation of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a deceased person who left insufficient funds to perform their obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this hadith to distinguish between Hajj al-Islam (the obligatory first pilgrimage) and voluntary Hajj, clarifying that insufficient funds for the former are treated as a debt to be settled from the estate, whereas funds for the latter remain with the heirs. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that Hajj al-Islam carries the weight of a financial obligation on the deceased, ensuring it is fulfilled before inheritance distribution.
